verdicts.title: Reduced motion hides every change chip: they sit at opacity 0 for their whole 1.7 s
verdicts.why: Reproduced on the frozen release build (1366x768, prefers-reduced-motion, Internal politics): the chips '−20' and '+2' are in the page from 43 ms to 1727 ms with computed opacity 0.00 in every frame (animation deltaFloat, duration 1e-06s); with full motion the same chips reach opacity 1. On a phone (390x844, test build, signed $40,000) the 'Closed this quarter' label is visibility:hidden from 48 ms to 1733 ms with nothing in its place, because app.css:273 hides it while a chip exists (pictures: test-results/audit/check-feel/f1-release-reduced-t0300.png, f1-phone-reduced-t0300.png; timelines f1-release-reduced.txt, f1-release-full.txt, f1-phone-reduced.txt). Cause confirmed in source: base.css:21 forces every animation to .001ms and deltaFloat (app.css:66-67) ends on opacity:0 with fill 'both'; it is the only in-game keyframe that ends hidden with no delay. Not intended: CHANGELOG.md:98 says 'A change to a number shows beside it for a moment', and base.css:19 ('People who ask for less get none') is about motion. The auditor slightly overstates 'no sign of what changed' (on a desktop the log line still lists the changes), but the chip is a designed feature that these players never see, and the phone label blink is a visible glitch. iOS Reduce Motion is a common setting.
verdicts.smallest_fix: src/styles/app.css, directly after line 67 (@keyframes deltaFloat): @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){ .delta{animation:none} }. Tried as a run-time style on the release build (desktop) and the test build (phone): chips at opacity 1.00 from the first frame until Kpis.jsx removes them at about 1.73 s (f1-fix-desktop-t0300.png, f1-fix-phone-t0300.png). No !important needed (base.css only forces durations), but the rule must come after the .delta rule.
verdicts.regression_risk: Very low. CSS only, no string, no engine, no save. No suite reads .delta (grep of test/). In reduced motion the chip now occupies the box it already occupies at full motion, so the layout suites see nothing new; the matrix suite's reduced-motion pass only looks at endings. Only seen in Chromium (the one engine installed), but it rests on standard fill-mode behaviour.

verdicts.title: A signed deal is the quietest line in the log: grey icon, while lost deals are red and warnings amber
verdicts.why: Facts hold: the close.signed line is rendered as class 'line' with icon colour rgb(130,138,150), the same grey as CRM cleanup; warn lines are rgb(226,179,64), bad lines rgb(240,112,108); .line.good (app.css:157) is styled and never emitted (Activity.jsx:8 and LogPeek.jsx:96 pass only bad and warn). But 'quietest' overstates it on a desktop: every log line has white text and only a 14 px icon carries colour, and the signing already gets two green chips, the count-up, the meter move, a green pace line and the cash sound in the same frame (f2-signed-t0400.png, f2-signed.txt). The one place it adds something is a phone with the stat cards scrolled away, where the notice, the cash sound and the strip's cash are the whole feedback (f2-phone-signed-t0500.png); a green handshake there is a small, quiet gain (tried in page: f2-try-phone-t0500.png, f2-try-desktop-t0500.png). No document records the grey as a decision, but the 2.1 implementation brief treats the log's colour as severity ('Week headers and log severity remain', docs/2.1/TTST_2.1_Claude_Code_Implementation.md:52), so a third colour is new vocabulary and a taste call; it would also leave ck.miracle, act.hail.chaosWon and qbr.hit grey.
verdicts.smallest_fix: Interface only: where a line's class is chosen (src/ui/app/Activity.jsx:8 and src/ui/app/LogPeek.jsx:96) add 'good' when e.tag is close.signed or ck.signed; app.css:157 does the rest. Do both or neither (Activity alone does nothing for the phone). Do not change the kind in src/game/deals.js:197: the engine is frozen and the kind is saved. Leaving it alone is defensible.
verdicts.regression_risk: Low. No test reads a log line's class (grep of test/e2e and test/parity). README and QA pictures that show a signing change by one icon colour. Colour comes from an existing token, so the colour lint is unaffected. Saves unchanged if the stored kind stays 'info'.

verdicts.title: The announcer marks CRM cleanup every time and a $40,000 signing never (the line is drawn at $45,000)
verdicts.why: The measurements are right: CRM cleanup plays crm and the PA chime at 35 ms, caption at 35 ms, voice at 756 ms; a $40,000 and a $44,999 signing play cash only; $45,000 adds 'Large sale verified. Ring something.' (f2-crm.txt, f2-signed.txt, f3-close-44999.txt, f3-close-45000.txt). But this is a tuning preference, not a defect. (1) The announcer is reserved for big moments by design: CHANGELOG.md:363 'Office PA announcer ... for week milestones, big events and endings'; CHANGELOG.md:354 names the 'Big-close PA line'; CHANGELOG.md:347 'Sounds and PA lines still fire on the same events'. The 45,000 line is unchanged since v1.14 (test/baseline/v1.21/index.html:2962 'if(amt >= 45000) r.say = "bigClose"') and is the audio suite's contract (test/audio/behaviour.test.mjs:76 'a big close is announced, a small one is not'; test/audio/golden/routing.json:414). (2) The proposal does not fix the asymmetry it describes: at 40,000 an ordinary $20,000 signing would still get no announcer while CRM cleanup gets one. It only changes batches worth $40,000 to $44,999, which is negligible. (3) The hygiene line on every cleanup is the joke, as the auditor says, and a recorded announcement that is stingy with praise is in voice (src/copy/pa.js:5). A signing is not silent: cash sound, green chips, count-up, meter.
verdicts.regression_risk: If changed anyway: the hand-written label 'close.signed >= 45000' in test/audio/behaviour.test.mjs:24 and test/audio/golden/routing.json:414 goes stale without failing; a one-line bank is heard more often; on a Friday it outranks the week's own line more often; it touches the sound engine in a pass that froze the 2.1 engine.

verdicts.title: clAInk's staged strike report is given away about two seconds early by the log, the phone notice and the change chips
verdicts.why: Reproduced on every surface (test build, fixtures ck-active-1-strike and ck-active-2-strikes). Desktop strike 2: the log reads 'Strike 2/3 (Procurement): ...' at 35 ms, the card and second box land at 2100 ms (f4-strike.txt, f4-strike-t0120.png). Damaging strike: chips '−$6,600' and '−$792' from 36 ms to 1728 ms, card at 2077 ms (f4-hurt.txt). Strike 3: 'Third strike. Seat revoked. Final true-up: $6,331 charged.' in the log at 47 ms, card at 2109 ms (f4-revoke.txt, f4-revoke-t0150.png). Phone: the notice announces the strike at 132 ms and stays until 3.65 s (strike 2) or 4.25 s (strike 3), sitting on top of the outcomes and 'Closed: $0' as they land (f4-phone-strike-t0300.png, f4-phone-strike-t2300.png, f4-phone-revoke-orig-t0400.png). The recorded intent is the opposite: CHANGELOG.md:240-242 'A run plays out in the workspace beat by beat ... The strike box fills when the strike card lands ... not while the agents are still "working"'. Nothing records that the notice (CHANGELOG.md:71, added in v2.0.1) should show a run's lines first, though LogPeek.jsx:13 does rank ck.* lines, so raising them was designed and only the clash with the staging was not handled. Worth doing for the phone notice only: there the notice is the one spoiler (the log and the stat cards are off screen) and it physically covers the report, so a one-line change restores the staging completely. Not worth doing on a desktop in this pass: at strike 3 the board itself gives it away at 47 ms (the deal leaves the list, cash counts down under a red chip, the cash line turns to 'Collections at −$1,500 cash', and the workspace drops its Run button and strike boxes and swaps − for × in its title bar), so holding the log lines would not complete the staging, and holding the state is not surgical.
verdicts.smallest_fix: Part (a) only. src/ui/app/LogPeek.jsx:59, where new lines are collected: skip the lines a clAInk run writes (ck.run, ck.signed, ck.miracle, ck.strike, ck.strike.hurt, ck.revoked, ck.farewell, ck.mgr.*; the RUN_TAGS of src/engine/audio/tagmap.js:57), e.g. one regex beside BIG. Tried on a scratch copy of the test build (test-results/audit/check-feel/test-patched-peek.html): no notice during a strike run on a 390x844 phone and the report plays uncovered (f4-phone-strike-patched-t2300.png); Prospect blitz still raises its notice. Leave Activity and the chips alone (the auditor's part (b) and the chip hold).
verdicts.regression_risk: (a) low: the notice checks in test/e2e/phone.cjs:114-124 and test/e2e/resilience.cjs section 7 use Prospect and End week, never a run; a run can only be started from the expanded workspace's own button (no shortcut, the button is inside the hidden body when minimized), so the workspace is on screen whenever lines are skipped; with reduced motion the report shows at once in the workspace. One loose end: at strike 3 the cash warning (pay.repoWarn) is not a run tag and still raises a one-line notice at 133 ms (f4-phone-revoke-patched.txt); skip it too when it shares a batch with a run, as director.js:16 does for sound, or accept it. The list must match RUN_TAGS. (b) medium, as the auditor says: the parity driver reads the log from the page (test/parity/drivers/next.cjs:199), resilience.cjs:115 looks 300 ms after a deploy, and a hold flag must be cleared on skip, unmount, New run and Load.

verdicts.title: Reaching quota is not marked: at 106% the meter is the same grey bar and the moment is an ordinary close
verdicts.why: Reproduced: $130,000 to $170,000 moves the meter 81.2% to 100% in about 150 ms, the fill is rgb(166,173,184) before and after, and the press plays the cash sound and nothing else (f5-quota.txt, f5-quota-t0900.png). It is a slight lack, not a fault: the card already reads '$170,000 106%' with a green '49 percentage points ahead of pace', and Kpis.jsx:51 states the design ('the words say it, the colour only repeats it'). A green bar at 100% is an addition, not a correction, so by the standard it is optional. Two things speak for it: it is one existing class with no motion, sound or copy (tried in page, reads well with the pace marker: f5-quota-try-t2200.png), and today nothing on the card says exactly when quota is reached, because the percentage label rounds up (see the missed item: '$159,500 100%' is under quota). If the label is fixed, the label itself marks the moment and the green bar becomes a nicety.
verdicts.smallest_fix: src/ui/app/Kpis.jsx:65: className={"meter" + (p.done >= 1 ? " good" : "")}. No sound and no line (the copydeck has none). Or leave alone.
verdicts.regression_risk: Low: colour only, no box changes, no test reads a meter's class. README and QA pictures of at-quota states change. It turns grey again if clAInk's churn strike claws revenue back under 100%, which is truthful. It must not be read as 'Club is safe' (a run at quota can still end by burnout, Collections or the 6% politics roll at manager under 25); it says only what 100% says.

verdicts.title: On a Friday with a choice, the week's change chips play dimmed under the dialog and are gone before it is answered
verdicts.why: Reproduced: End week into the pricing dialog opens it at 56 ms; chips '+15', '−4' and '+$1,000' run from 76 ms to 1743 ms under the backdrop (f6-friday-dialog.txt, f6-friday-dialog-t0400.png; they are faintly legible through it). The loss is negligible: these are Friday's routine changes, which the cards announce before the press ('+15 on Friday', 'Eases 4 on Friday') and the log lists afterwards, and the choice's own effects still get their chips once it is made. A Friday signing coinciding with a choice dialog is rare (a 15% Friday close with an 18% or 10% event) and still gets its log line and the cash sound. The fix is a behaviour change, not a repair: it alters useDelta for every dialog, including clAInk's manager acknowledgement that waits for the report, and merges Friday's change and the choice's into one number. The auditor concedes that leaving it is defensible.
verdicts.regression_risk: If attempted: chip timing changes in every week with a dialog; a held baseline that is never released if some path does not clear waiting(s); a late combined chip after the clAInk acknowledgement; the count-up would still run under the dialog, so chip and number would disagree in time.

verdicts.title: A stage change is applied in one frame with no mark on the rows that moved
verdicts.why: The observation is accurate (Discovery, three leads: all three rows go Lead to Qualified at 29 ms; the only animations running are the energy chip, the meter widths and the button's hover transition; f7-discovery.txt), but it is not a shortcoming by the studio's standard. The change is already carried four ways in the first frame: the pips and stage name in place, the count badges on the action buttons, the log line 'Discovery: 3 deals qualified.' and the typewriter sound. That meets the requirement, so it is verified, not lacking. The proposal adds motion to a deliberately still dashboard, replays on every stage cell whenever the list is first drawn, and does nothing on the long board where the moved rows are below the fold, which is the only case the auditor shows as weak. The auditor rates it a nit with low confidence and says leaving it alone is reasonable; agreed.
verdicts.regression_risk: If attempted: every stage cell animates on load and New run; layout and matrix suites measure boxes that would carry a 4 px transform for 0.32 s; keying a cell on stage remounts it and can drop a title tooltip mid-hover.

missed.title: The stat card rounds the share of quota up across the lines that decide the ending: it says 100% (or 70%) and the QBR then says 99% (69%) and ends the run on that
missed.where: src/copy/ui.js:4 and :53 (KPI.ofQuota uses pc, which is Math.round), drawn by src/ui/app/Kpis.jsx:64; against src/game/quarter.js:23 (qbr.final floors) and :25 (Club needs perfQ >= 1), src/game/selectors.js:80 (the ending card floors), and the copydeck's note on qbr.final, docs/2.1/TTST_2.1_Editorial_Copydeck.md:160: 'do not round actual threshold across 70/100'.
missed.evidence: Release build, $159,500 closed of a $160,000 quota: the card reads '$159,500 100%' over a bar that looks full (test-results/audit/check-feel/f5-just-under.png). Test build, week 13, quiet dice: the card reads '$159,500, 100%', 'On pace', 'Expected by Friday: 100% of quota'; End week then logs 'Q1 final: 99% of quota.' and 'Under quota. Badge access renewed.' and opens the missed ending (m1-round-qbr.txt in the same folder). Same at the firing line: card '$111,500, 70%', then 'Q1 final: 69% of quota.', 'Below 70% of quota. HR has prepared the paperwork.', ending fired (m1-round-70.txt). The bands are narrow ($159,200 to $159,999; $111,200 to $111,999; likewise just under 80%), but this is the number the game is about, a player can be misled by it in week 13, and it is why nothing on the card marks reaching quota (the auditor's fifth finding). No document records the card's rounding as a decision; the log line and the ending card both floor.
missed.proposal: In KPI.ofQuota only (src/copy/ui.js:53): never round up onto 70, 80 or 100 when the share is still below it (show 69, 79, 99). Do not simply floor the label: the pace line's points are rounded from the same share, so a floored label would sit one point off 'N percentage points ahead of pace' in about half of all states (today 38% against 10% expected reads 28 points, and adds up). Leave pc and 'Expected by Friday' alone. Risk: low; no test asserts this label (grep of test/), the format stays 'N%', no copydeck string changes; inside the three narrow bands the label and the pace points can differ by one.
